items.title: Alfred Williams Interview, 1961-10-13
items.q: And me, him, Vernon Gilbert, Tillman. Playing what? Tillman playing bass, you know.

ctx.x: So, who would he have in his dance band when you first joined?

Vernon Gilbert. And me, him, Vernon Gilbert, Tillman. Playing what? Tillman playing bass, you know. Mm-hmm. Bass horn, you know, like he playing the Vernon Gilbert trumpet. You know, clarinet. And, um, well, he had a saxophonian, Handy playing with him. Pretty good while, Handy playing with him a good while. Um, and after Handy stopped playing with him, and I had Harold. Mm-hmm. Harold been playing with him. He was Smitty on piano. And he used the piano, you know what I'm saying? Did he use a guitar player…
That's not the same as Raymond Clifford. No, no.

Now, the only time they would play short, they'd play orchestration, you see. Well, they'd play it down. And if it was a good orchestration, you know, that they liked, well, they'd go back to the chorus and play one or two, you see. Of course, Celestine always read music, just like Manuel Perez, you see. Always had musicians in their reach, you know. It felt like Buddy Pettine, you know.

You know, when I used to go out to Tyler's Beer Garden? Who? To Tyler's Beer Garden during the war. I don't think you were ever out there. No, I don't. But Joe Avery and Wilbur Tillman had the band. Tillman played with us?
